title: Circular Motion and Simple Harmonic Motion
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Physics: Circular Motion and Oscillations Worksheets
standard_text: Circular motion (angular speed, centripetal acceleration and force) and simple harmonic motion (defining equation, the mass–spring system and simple pendulum, maximum speed and acceleration).
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level physics worksheets on circular motion and simple harmonic motion: angular speed, centripetal force, mass–spring systems, pendulums and SHM equations. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

An object moving in a circle at constant speed accelerates towards the centre: a = v²/r = ω²r, with ω = 2πf = v/r. The resultant (centripetal) force is F = mv²/r.

In simple harmonic motion a = −ω²x. The maximum speed is ωA and the maximum acceleration is ω²A. A mass on a spring: T = 2π√(m/k); a pendulum: T = 2π√(l/g).

Example

Mass 0.5 kg on a 50 N/m spring. Period?

T = 2π√(0.5/50)

Answer: 0.628 s

Example

A = 0.05 m, f = 2 Hz. Maximum speed?

ω = 4π = 12.6 rad/s

v = ωA

Answer: 0.628 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Using f instead of ω = 2πf.
  • Thinking centripetal force is a separate extra force.
  • Using degrees in x = A cos ωt.

faq.a: The resultant force towards the centre that keeps an object moving in a circle: F = mv²/r.
Acceleration proportional to displacement and directed towards the equilibrium position: a = −ω²x.
